The binding date is the one each embassy or consulate general sets for its own country.

official.application_route: Apply through the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality with one original packet and one copy packet; that mission runs the First Screening and recommends you to MEXT, which runs the Second Screening and assigns the university. official.study_mode: Full-time; the academic year runs from 1 April to 31 March and the preparatory course is a one-year intensive course in the Japanese language and other subjects
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. An applicant holding Japanese nationality at the time of application is not eligible, except dual nationals resident outside Japan who choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality by the date of arrival in Japan; the First Screening must be conducted at the mission of the chosen nationality.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is for international students; applicants must not hold Japanese nationality at the time of application, and dual nationals must verify they will relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must choose a Field of Study - either Social Sciences and Humanities (course A or B) or Natural Sciences (course A, B or C) - plus a course and up to three majors, entering a first, second and third choice. Fields of art, including music, are not majors eligible for application, and those choosing 'Others' in Humanities - A may have difficulty finding universities that can accept them.
official.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory education; seven years until March 2034 for grantees majoring in medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year course in pharmacy; four years (six for those majors) for a grantee who enrols through direct placement. The scholarship period may be extended on successful MEXT examination for grantees admitted to a master's or doctoral course with outstanding academic achievement.
official.description: MEXT offers scholarships to international students who wish to study at Japanese national universities as Undergraduate Students under the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship Program, with the stated aim of fostering human resources who will become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan and who will contribute to the development of both countries and the wider world.
official.region: Global, limited to the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan
official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL minimum score is published. English is examined as a written academic examination subject in the First Screening - English (A) for Social Sciences and Humanities - A, English (B) for Social Sciences and Humanities - B and for all Natural Sciences courses - and a certificate of English-language ability is submitted only if the applicant already holds one, as a copy issued no earlier than two years before the date of application.

applicant_utility.summary: MEXT's undergraduate embassy-recommendation award is a five-year commitment, not a one-off grant: one intensive year of Japanese and foundation subjects at ABK College (Social Sciences and Humanities) or Osaka University (Natural Sciences), then a bachelor's degree at a national university that MEXT assigns - you do not choose the university. Your real counterpart is the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your own country, which sets the deadline, collects the two application packets, runs the written academic examinations and the interview, and only then recommends you to MEXT for the Second Screening. Budget for the gap as well: accommodation, local transport to the departure airport, airport taxes, travel insurance and baggage are all yours, and MEXT advises arriving with roughly US$2,000 because the first monthly payment lands one to one-and-a-half months after you arrive.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers and recent secondary-school graduates under 25 who want a tuition-free, Japanese-medium bachelor's degree in Japan and can accept a year of intensive language study before the degree begins.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality before anything else - it owns the deadline, the examination dates and the list of courses offering direct placement, and all of these differ by country
Confirm you will be 18 or older at university admission and that you will complete 12 years of schooling by March 2027
Order a school-issued transcript covering every year with the grade scale shown, plus a graduation or prospective-graduation certificate
Book a physician who will complete MEXT's prescribed health certificate form - a generic hospital letter is not accepted
Ask your last school's principal or class teacher for a free-format recommendation letter, using MEXT's published sample as a guide
Assemble two complete packets, one original set and one copy set, numbered 1 to 9 in the top right corner of each first page, and translate every document not already in Japanese or English
common_rejection_risks: Age cut-off: applicants must in principle have been born on or after 2 April 2002, and personal circumstances such as financial, family, health, university or employment situations are never accepted as exceptions
Failing or not sitting the written academic examinations - Japanese, English, mathematics plus chemistry and physics or chemistry and biology depending on field - which every applicant takes
Simultaneously applying for another MEXT scholarship programme, including any whose payments begin in FY2026 or FY2027, which makes you ineligible here
Already holding, or planning to hold, 'Student' residence status in Japan before the scholarship payment period starts
Being a previous MEXT scholarship grantee, including anyone who withdrew after acquiring student status
Naming a fine-arts or music major, which the guidelines exclude from application altogether
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation - preparatory institution residences and university international student halls are available but the grantee pays and rooms are limited - domestic travel from home to the departure airport, airport taxes and usage fees, transit and in-Japan travel costs, travel insurance, carry-on and unaccompanied baggage, and daily living costs until the first payment arrives, for which MEXT suggests approximately US$2,000.
document_audit: The health certificate must be on MEXT's FY2027 prescribed form and signed by a physician; a hospital letterhead document will not do
Transcripts must show the grade scale and grades for every subject in every year, and current students must submit a final transcript again at graduation
Language proficiency certificates are only submitted if you already hold one, must be copies rather than originals, and must be issued within two years of your application date
Documents submitted in bound form may be dismantled during review, so do not rely on binding to keep your packet intact
The photograph must be 4.5 x 3.5 cm, taken within six months, upper-body and full-faced with no hat, with your name and nationality written on the back

A certificate of university enrolment qualification examination, where applicable, can replace the transcript, graduation certificate and recommendation letter - check whether your situation qualifies before assembling all of them
alerts: The FY2027 round's April-May 2026 recruitment window and May-August 2026 First Screening have already passed, so treat this cycle as closed and watch the official page for the next round rather than mailing documents now
Documents sent directly to MEXT in Japan are ignored - everything goes through your diplomatic mission
Arriving outside the specified period, entering Japan without a newly obtained 'Student' visa, or changing to another residence status suspends payment and forfeits return airfare
A false statement on the application or cheating in the written examination can force you to return part or all of the scholarship already paid

Direct placement is discretionary, only for applicants MEXT judges to have sufficient Japanese language ability, and the consultation window runs only until 12 February 2027; if no university accepts you, you enrol at the preparatory institution instead
Grantees must enrol in National Health Insurance on arrival, and those testing positive for infectious diseases including tuberculosis must be fully treated before arrival
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Contact your Japanese diplomatic mission, download the FY2027 forms, submit an original packet plus a copy packet by the mission's deadline, sit the mission's written examinations and interview, then await the First Screening result before MEXT's Second Screening and university placement decision.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-year, non-degree Japanese Studies Program at a designated Japanese university, and it is explicitly conditional on going home: you must return by the end of the final month of the scholarship period and resume Japanese language and culture study at the university you left, or you can be ordered to repay the entire scholarship retroactively. The course catalogue is closed - you may only choose universities listed in MEXT's Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program, and MEXT, not you, decides the placement. You already need roughly a year of Japanese-study credits and enough Japanese to be taught in Japanese, because the First Screening includes a written examination in Japanese with no English component at all. Placement for the FY2026 round had to be settled by 14 August 2026, so that cycle is closed; the value of this record is in understanding the exact shape of the next round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Undergraduates already majoring in Japanese language or culture at a university outside Japan, with at least one year of Japanese-study credits and a home department that will take them back afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify against your transcript that you will have a full year of Japanese language and culture study completed by 1 September 2026, and mark those courses on the transcript you submit
Read MEXT's Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program before touching the preference form and note the Japanese proficiency level each university requires
Agree a return-and-continue plan with your home university's president or academic advisor at the application stage, since the recommendation letter comes from them
Confirm with your home university whether credits earned in Japan will transfer back to your degree
Prepare for a written examination in Japanese rather than English, plus an interview at your diplomatic mission
Check the course guide whether your chosen universities require accommodation fees to be paid before you arrive in Japan
common_rejection_risks: Not returning to the home institution and continuing Japanese study, which can trigger an order to repay the whole scholarship retroactively
Less than one year of Japanese language and culture study at university by 1 September 2026 - the guidelines state such applicants are not eligible to apply
Majoring in something other than Japanese language or culture and only taking Japan-related electives, which the guidelines specifically exclude
No accepting university determined by the specified date - 14 August 2026 for the FY2026 round - which results in automatic rejection
Being a previous MEXT scholarship grantee, or concurrently applying for another MEXT programme including a university-recommended Japanese Studies Students award for FY2026
Arriving without a newly obtained 'Student' visa, accepting another Japanese government or government-related scholarship, or changing to another residence status after arrival
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, which some universities require to be paid in advance of arrival, domestic travel to the departure airport, airport taxes and usage fees, transit and in-Japan travel costs, travel insurance, carry-on and excess baggage, and living costs before the first payment - MEXT advises bringing approximately US$2,000.

A separate verification document is needed only if your current university's transcript does not already prove a full year of Japanese study

The certificate of Japanese language ability, if submitted, must be a copy showing your name and level or score and issued no earlier than two years before application
The recommendation letter should be requested from your current university's head or academic advisor, who must also be briefed on your post-return study plan

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality with the FY2026 original packet and copy packet by the mission's deadline, sit the Japanese written examination and interview, then await MEXT's Second Screening and the notification of your accepting university.
